title: Comment stripper
brief: Copy C source to the output with its comments removed. Remove /* block */ comments, which can span lines, and // line comments, but keep the newline at the end of a line comment. Text inside a "string" is not a comment, so leave it alone.

tests.name: An escaped quote in a string

hints: A regular expression for a block comment is hard to get right. Use a start condition instead: %x COMMENT.
On "/*" run BEGIN(COMMENT). Inside, match "*/" to go back with BEGIN(INITIAL), and throw away everything else with <COMMENT>.|\n.
A second start condition for strings keeps comment markers inside them safe. Remember that \" does not end a string.
explanation: Start conditions turn the scanner into a small state machine: normal text, inside a comment, inside a string. Each state has its own rules, which is much clearer than one huge regular expression. It also avoids the classic mistake of "/*".*"*/", which uses longest match to swallow everything up to the last comment in the file.
